_doc: Grand Junction Motor Speedway through Lake Murray v4's engine (ledger 0078). The line, widths and profile are tracks/grand-junction's (installed 0.3.0), read by tools/lm_engine_intake.py; the profile is the measured one with the elevation stage's grade cap undone; the camber is the G10 lidar survey (source/lidar/camber-survey/crossfall.json); the 3DEP grid is this port's own fetch (the live track commits none); the edge is the circuit's (no curb, no sidewalk). Every other key is the live track's, copied; the live config is untouched.

source._smooth_window_doc: 2026-11-01 (ledger 0060, High Plains' lesson): source/osm_fixes.json is a list of 53 OSM nodes (5.7 m apart on the corners, up to 149 m on the straights), not a 1 Hz GPS drive; from_track's 5-fix moving average put the line 5.74 m median / 10.95 p95 / 14.36 m max off the source polygon, i.e. every one of the 11 corners cut by more than the 9.75 m road, and shortened the lap 1,321 -> 1,130 m (the V1 builds of ledger 0018 drove 1,032 m). 0 = no smoothing: the line is the OSM polygon resampled at 3 m (build_mesh still corner-rounds it for the sweep). The closing 127 m (last node -> first) is the east straight's own segment (0.4 / 3.1 deg turn at its ends), not a chord.
source._note: Real OSM highway=raceway way 293789503 at 3002 N I-70 Frontage Rd, Grand Junction CO (Mesa County). Closed 54-node ring, native CCW winding reversed to CW. ROAD COURSE (~0.9 mi advertised, 11 turns, ~9.75 m/32 ft wide asphalt sprint/kart circuit). Flat mesa-top site north of I-70; elevation from USGS 3DEP bare-earth (do NOT flatten); NO banking. A '1.25-mi oval/banked' web claim was a conflation with other venues and is rejected.

road_profile._doc: 1.03 km purpose-built circuit on flat Grand Valley ground. 3DEP sampled every 3 m over a lap this short is mostly DEM surface noise, and the 33 m default median cannot reject it: 130-236 kinks/km against a 3%-slope-change threshold, i.e. a jagged deck everywhere rather than a few bad spots. Same lever that fixed Second Creek. A graded racetrack is smooth by construction; the profile should be too.
road_profile._fold_pads_doc: 2026-11-03 (ledger 0074, Aspen's mechanism): the first chain run laid fold pads at all 4 hairpin apexes (flat zones r 20.88 m at apex heights 0.64 / 1.35 / 3.92 / 5.52 m) and their rims were steps - severe 41 at 569-575 and 1,008-1,014 m, kinks 116.5 /km, steps 60.6 /km. No disc, no flat zone; the engine's +-40 m fold plateau stays.

route._orientation_doc: Research 2026-07-20: GJMS deliberately runs BOTH directions by event; CW is the default (LapMeta primary variation). Our ring is CW. S/F on the east-side main straight beside the paddock (~39.1087,-108.4918), CW = heading south into the SE hairpin. Pit lane parallel on the east (paddock) side, ~150 m, openings both ends. A CCW layout variant is a future option (reverse: true).

edge._grass_clearance_doc: 0.1.2 (PC, 2026-11-09; Kevin, asked whether the other circuit tracks have Milford's fast-curve edge mess: "Yes, check them"; Milford 0.1.6 is the same fix, ledger 0087): the strip's outer lip 2 cm under the lane edge (profile point 3 at -grass_clearance = +0.08 over the unlifted edge; the lane edge at +0.10). engine-july's prep holds the ground past the ROAD edge at the lane edge's height - 0.02 for 3 m (its contact band), so the lower lip lay in a gutter with a wall of ground at its lip. Measured on the installed 0.1.1 (gate OBJ, every 10 m, both sides; strip_gutter.py): the strip's lip 14 cm under the lane edge; the ground just past it stood more than 5 cm over the lip at 46 of 218 side-stations, more than 10 cm at 17 (max 12 cm). Flush with the band, nothing stands over it
edge._doc: the circuit edge (ledger 0078): no curb, no sidewalk. The asphalt edge is held at road height for 0.30 m and the run-off ground meets it 0.15 m lower over 1.0 m [invented: the flush meet the drive gate reads as no drop]; the ground beyond is the assembler's conform to the road, then the 3DEP surface: the real run-off level.

Ledger 0018 / 0031's 'rough everywhere, mechanism not found' was measured on that corner-cut line; the chain's draft on the real polygon is the first new thing to try (ONE-CHAIN §4).

road_wear._doc: ledger 0084 (Kevin 2026-11-07: "road textures to include wear along where tires run, in a realistic manner" / "For tracks we'll use racing lines" / "Which will help darken curbs realistically"; 2026-11-10, to the Mac: "build the road wear for the other circuits on the pc overnight", then "Tone only, no rubber"). High Plains 0.1.7's bake (tools/road_wear_blend.py, last in prep): the large-scale tone off the aerial, registered to the built road, under the stock cracked asphalt kept as the 4 m detail (ksPerPixelMultiMap_NMDetail); tone only, no rubber (rubber 'none': no band drawn, the photo's tone as it is). scripts/aerial/road_wear.py DEFAULTS has every number, marked measured / model / invented.
road_wear._surfaces_doc: the road and the edge strip beside it (ledger 0087's 1KERB_sidewalk), as Milford and High Plains: the strip shares the atlas so the rubber where the line clips the edge carries on over it
road_wear._texel_doc: as High Plains 0.1.7: 0.25 m keeps the detail multiplier whole (4096 px x 0.25 / 4 = 256; the bake refuses a fractional one) and is finer than a 0.3 m photo's pixel
road_wear._rubber_doc: Kevin 2026-11-10, to the Mac, asked "Pueblo, Aspen, Grand Junction and Pikes Peak show no rubber: tone only, or the drawn band?": "Tone only, no rubber" (ledger 0084, runbook 0084-3). The asphalt bakes the photo's tone with no band drawn (scripts/aerial/road_wear.rubber_mode); the line and the photo's line-vs-mirror depth are still measured and recorded (data/road_wear.line.<layout>.json), and the gate's no_rubber row needs the shipped atlas's depth within photo_depth_tol 0.02 of the photo's own: the atlas adds no band. The overnight photo-mode build (0.1.3) measured the photo's own depth 0.002, under photo_min_depth 0.03.
